stories.headline: OpenAI corrects billing error, effectively tightening GPT-6.2 usage caps
stories.confirmed_fact: OpenAI has corrected a billing error that incorrectly discounted usage for its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models. As a result, paying users will now reach their usage caps 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than they did during the launch week.
stories.why_it_matters: For power users and businesses relying on these models, the change represents a significant reduction in the effective allowance per subscription, despite OpenAI's claims regarding the models' token efficiency.
stories.interpretation: The correction highlights the gap between initial launch-day expectations and the actual operational costs of running newer, more resource-intensive models.
stories.source_title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)

stories.headline: Anthropic researcher compresses formal proof of Riemann Hypothesis
stories.confirmed_fact: Anthropic researcher Luke Sernau has released a compact, open-source Lean 4 repository that reduces a 17-million-line formal proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis to approximately 76,000 lines. The proof has passed standard Lean kernel validation.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a notable step in AI-assisted mathematics, demonstrating that machine-generated proofs can be distilled into more manageable, verifiable forms without losing logical integrity.
stories.interpretation: While the proof is logically consistent within the Lean environment, the real test remains the ongoing effort by mathematicians to translate this into a human-readable format.
stories.source_title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic

stories.headline: Institutional investors offload 2021-era VC stakes to fund AI bets
stories.confirmed_fact: Institutional investors, including pension funds and university endowments, are selling their positions in 2021-era venture capital funds on the secondary market at steep discounts. The liquidity generated is being redirected toward new AI-focused technology funds.
stories.why_it_matters: This trend signals a broader reallocation of capital as institutional LPs attempt to exit the high-valuation vintage of 2021 to chase the current wave of AI investment.
stories.interpretation: The willingness to accept knockdown prices suggests that these investors view the potential upside of current AI-focused funds as worth the immediate loss on their legacy portfolios.
stories.source_title: Analysis: institutional investors are selling stakes in older VC funds from the 2021 investment boom peak at steep discounts and rushing to back new AI funds (Financial Times)

stories.headline: New York Times restricts Photoshop 2027 updates for staff photographers
stories.confirmed_fact: The New York Times has directed contributing photographers to avoid updating to Adobe Photoshop 2027 (v28.0.0+) due to concerns over automated generative AI features that operate without explicit prompts and embed C2PA metadata.
stories.why_it_matters: The move highlights the tension between new AI-powered creative tools and the strict provenance requirements necessary for maintaining journalistic integrity.
stories.interpretation: Institutional resistance to these features is likely to grow as media organisations prioritise image authenticity over the convenience of automated editing tools.
stories.source_title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features

practical_takeaway: If you are a heavy user of OpenAI's latest models, expect your monthly usage limits to feel tighter than they did last week. For those in creative or data-sensitive industries, consider auditing your software update policies to ensure that new AI-integrated tools do not inadvertently alter your metadata or workflow standards.
watch_next: Keep an eye on how other major media outlets respond to Adobe's automated AI features, and monitor whether the secondary market for 2021-era VC funds continues to show signs of distress as more capital flows into AI.
